title: Unauthenticated ASP.NET / API settings write
summary: Prove missing [Authorize] on Settings/Save* writes with a paired 401 sibling vs 200 void.
steps: Map POST/PUT Save*/Write*/Settings endpoints from crawl, JS, or OpenAPI (e.g. /api/Settings/SaveSettings).
Baseline: unauth POST a sibling write that should be protected (/api/TaskAdmin/UpdateTask or similar) with use_auth_session=false. Expect 401.

Mutant: unauth POST SaveSettings with one canary key (aegis-verify-<rand>) matching the settings schema (pass json= body). Do not send a replacement settings collection. Do not flip enableNotifications/createPlannerTasks/powerBIReportId.
PASS: sibling 401 AND SaveSettings 200 with Content-Length: 0 (ASP.NET Core void success). GET GetSettings 500 / NullReferenceException is NOT a kill.
submit_finding_candidate High with the paired statuses. queue_finding_followups(vuln_type='unauth_settings_write').
Then probe LogQuery/Audit/ReadTasks/OpenDocument without 401 as a sibling missing-auth card — empty arrays and Graph 500s are not this write.
pass_signals: Protected sibling write returns 401 without Authorization
